question_or_symptom: A shared session can receive a valid earlier completion while another queue, memory, or signal request is awaiting its ACK, but broad buffering can hide a completion for the active request or a foreign signal.
observation: HELLO seeds one strictly increasing request-ID tracker shared by queue, memory, and signal records. Only canonical completions for previously ACKed pending work may interleave; an active request completion, duplicate, foreign identity, unknown record, or noncanonical result is a protocol failure. Unknown correlatable signal opcodes return a deterministic MALFORMED ACK that echoes the raw opcode.
conclusion: Interleaving is safe only with one correlation namespace and an allowlist tied to acknowledged work, not a generic completion buffer.
decision: Consume request IDs after structural/version/identity/capability admission even for deterministic lifecycle failures, validate every completion against its acknowledged owner and request record, buffer only canonical allowed completions, and preserve deterministic raw-opcode failure echoes.
invalidated_assumptions: Queue, memory, and signal request counters can advance independently on one connection.
Any well-formed completion is harmless to buffer while a synchronous ACK is pending.
